newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to meet Maastricht criteria on time - Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: Germany to meet Maastricht criteria on time - Kinkel.

text.p: Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said Germany would fulfill the Maastricht criteria for monetary union (EMU) on time and urged political leaders talking about different budget deficit figures to show more responsibility.

In an interview with the Neue Osnabruecker Zeitung newspaper published on Tuesday, Kinkel said Germany would fulfill the deficit criterion for monetary union as well as other fiscal targets as spelled out in the Maastricht Treaty.
"We will fulfill the debt criterion and the other criteria," Kinkel said.
The Maastricht Treaty states that European Union countries hoping to qualify for monetary union when it is launched in 1999 must meet certain fiscal targets this year.

The treaty says public sector deficits must not exceed three percent of gross domestic product, but a debate is raging in Germany over whether this means 3.0 percent exactly, or perhaps allows for a slight overshooting.
"I have always been opposed to the decimal point discussion. People should just take a look at what is in the Maastricht Treaty. What is written there is what is required," said Kinkel.
"I repeat -- we will enter the euro on time by achieving the criteria," he added.

Kinkel also said that the planned enlargements of NATO and the European Union would not mean Germany would contribute more funds to the two institutions. In fact Kinkel said Germany should in the future pay less to the EU.
He said Germany contributes about 600 million marks each year for NATO and "I assume that this will not increase by any considerable amount."
Kinkel said increased costs through the enlargement of the EU needs to be a defrayed through a realignment of funds.

"The existing financial framework will not change," Kinkel said. "There needs to be a new distribution. We want to make sure that with the new alignment that Germany, which so far has been by far the largest net contributer, comes out more favourably in the future."
